summary: The image-worker Deployment now uses the node's network namespace. It also mounts the node's Docker socket so each conversion can run in its own container.

findings.title: Node Docker socket mounted into worker pod
findings.problem: The Deployment mounts the host's /var/run/docker.sock into the worker container. Any process holding that socket can drive the node's Docker daemon as root.
findings.consequence: An attacker who compromises the worker can start a privileged container and take over the node. This bypasses runAsNonRoot, dropped capabilities and seccomp, and exposes every pod and secret on that node.
findings.fix: Remove the docker volume and volumeMount. Run conversions as Kubernetes Jobs, or use a sandboxed runner such as rootless BuildKit or a gVisor runtime class.

findings.title: Worker pod shares the node network namespace
findings.problem: The worker pod sets hostNetwork to true just to reach a cache on the node's localhost. The pod then shares the node's network namespace and bypasses pod NetworkPolicies.
findings.consequence: A compromised worker can reach every service bound to node localhost, including kubelet and daemon ports. It can also observe other pods' traffic on that node.
findings.fix: Remove hostNetwork. Reach the image cache through a node-local Service, or at the node IP from the downward API.
